correctness.rationale: The complete Delsarte formula is transformed using Gaussian reciprocity. Even-rank pattern insertion yields a coefficientwise-positive difference; its first term counts a+1 split jumps and a+2 first omitted patterns. Odd-rank defect bounds and identical central transitions prove eventual affine behavior. Leading/subleading coefficients are enumerated from all defect zero/one terms. 49 complete-polynomial and 28 sharp-boundary exact checks independently confirm bounded cases; they are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Aivazidis arXiv:2606.03320v1 Theorem A, Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 9.1 give Delsarte normalization, insertion, leading coefficients and the limiting product. The new claim is the sharp finite-exponent coefficientwise boundary with universal first shortfall 2a+3 and the all-codegree eventual-affine odd-rank law. The proof counts missing noncentral patterns and central-switch placements, rather than reproducing the known limiting bound. Prior specialized exact rank-four enumeration may imply cases, but no available source establishes the all-rank statement.
residual_risks: Exact rank-four formulas might imply selected coefficient identities, even though the all-rank theorem is broader; full paper unavailable.
Older q-series or Hall-polynomial identities could imply the precise congruence and sharp boundary without using these words.
Priority is an evidence-based self-review, not a mathematical proof of nonexistence of earlier results.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an effective optimal coefficient cutoff and a rank-universal first discrepancy for an entire infinite family of natural subgroup-count polynomials, sharpening a recently studied analytic limiting factor to finite-exponent coefficient behavior. Its odd-rank analogue bounds every fixed top coefficient by eventual affine complexity, with a uniform explicit stabilization range; this parity dichotomy is structural, not a cherry-picked small table or cosmetic rephrasing.
